mistakes.why: Dirty brushes drag grit across the paint and leave swirl marks.

mistakes.why: Dry wiping grinds dust into the clear coat.

mistakes.why: Soap dries on hot paint and leaves spots.

myths.truth: It makes washing faster and easier. You still wash.

myths.truth: Rain leaves minerals and dirt behind when it dries.

tips.why: The grit stays in the rinse bucket instead of going back on the paint.

tips.tip: Vacuum before you wipe anything down

tips.tip: Clean the glass last with its own towel

questions.a: A full detail every 4 to 6 months and a wash every couple of weeks. More often with kids, pets or street parking.

questions.q: How long does a full detail take?
questions.a: Most full details take a few hours. A very dirty interior takes longer.

questions.q: Can you get pet hair out of car seats?
questions.a: Yes. A rubber brush and a strong vacuum pull most of it out. Deep carpet takes longer.

questions.q: What is the difference between a car wash and a detail?
questions.a: A wash is the outside surface. A detail is every surface, inside and out, plus protection.

compare.point: A handyman takes small jobs and lists. A contractor runs big projects.
DIY costs your weekend and your tools. Hiring costs money and saves both.

questions.q: How much does a handyman cost?
questions.a: It depends on the jobs and the time. Many charge by the hour or by the job.

questions.q: What can a handyman do?
questions.a: Repairs, mounting, assembly, painting and small fixes. Licensed trades handle big electrical and plumbing.

questions.q: Should I hire a handyman or a contractor?
questions.a: Small jobs and lists go to a handyman. Big projects go to a contractor.

questions.q: How do I get a fair quote?
questions.a: Send photos and a clear list. Ask what is included.

questions.q: Can a handyman mount a TV?
questions.a: Yes. Ask about the wall type and the mount.
